registry.description: Surrender is the giving up of self-governance — the inner act of letting go of one's claim to control one's own life, resources, or outcome. The Hebrew vocabulary here is built around the root for closing, shutting, and the coming out that happens when a city falls to a siege: surrender is what happens when resistance ends. In Scripture, surrender to God is not defeat but the beginning of genuine life: the self that is surrendered to God is not destroyed but restored. The theology of surrender runs through the entire biblical account of what it means to trust.
registry.inference_note: Surrender as a spiritual concept — the yielding of the will to God — is ABSENT as a single biblical term. The concept is expressed through several yielding and presenting terms.

terms.medium_def:
: come/go out/escape
1) to go out, come out, exit, go forth
1a) (Qal)
1a1) to go or come out or forth, depart
1a2) to go forth (to a place)
1a3) to go forward, proceed to (to or toward something)
1a4) to come or go forth (with purpose or for result)
1a5) to come out of
1b) (Hiphil)
1b1) to cause to go or come out, bring out, lead out
1b2) to bring out of
1b3) to lead out
1b4) to deliver
1c) (Hophal) to be brought out or forth

terms.medium_def:
: issue/flow/sprouting/leaping(water/fire/OBJECTS)
1) to go out, come out, exit, go forth
1a) (Qal)
1a1) to go or come out or forth, depart
1a2) to go forth (to a place)
1a3) to go forward, proceed to (to or toward something)
1a4) to come or go forth (with purpose or for result)
1a5) to come out of
1b) (Hiphil)
1b1) to cause to go or come out, bring out, lead out
1b2) to bring out of
1b3) to lead out
1b4) to deliver
1c) (Hophal) to be brought out or forth
